newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa plans 2ce daily HK-Germany cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans 2ce daily HK-Germany cargo flights.

text.p: Lufthansa said it expects to increase its Hong Kong-Frankfurt Boeing 747 freighter flights in conjunction with partner Cathay Pacific to 12 from 11 per week later this year.
And the intention is to operate a twice-daily 747F service within two years, said Lufthansa executive board member, Stefan Lauer.

Speaking to reporters in Hong Kong, Lauer said Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport ranked fifth in the airline's tonnage rankings on its worldwide network and that Lufthansa was the leading cargo carrier between southern China and Europe.
Lauer said Lufthansa Cargo generated more than double the airline's passenger revenue on the Hong Kong-Frankfurt route.
Hong Kong and China traffic also accounted for 24 percent of total business in Asia, Lufthansa said.
"Two of our 11 freighters are dedicated to Hong Kong, which gives you some idea of how the market is developing," stated Lauer.

"We are in discussion with Cathay now about starting a 12th frequency in the autumn and subject to demand, we hope to go double daily within 12 to 24 months. This reinforces our confidence in the future growth potential of Hong Kong and beyond markets," Lauer said.

He added that Lufthansa Cargo was now asking its customers to tell the autonomous division about their expectations so it could prepare overfly rights and secure landing rights prior to beginning new services.
Lufthansa and Cathay have been operating a cargo joint venture on the Hong Kong-Frankfurt route via either Sharjah or Dubai for the past 15 years.
The last increase in capacity was made in April when Lufthansa began its sixth weekly frequency, bringing the current joint total to 11 per week.
